The Independent National Electoral Commission and the Rivers State Police Command have restated their resolve to prevent electoral violence and disruptions during the 2027 general elections. The two institutions also pledged stronger inter-agency collaboration to guarantee a peaceful and secure environment ahead of the elections. Stakeholders stressed the need for intelligence sharing, strategic security deployment and coordinated action to tackle potential threats before, during and after the elections. They made the commitment during a meeting of the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security, held at the INEC State Office along Aba Road in Port Harcourt on Tuesday. The state Resident Electoral Commissioner, Dr Johnson Sinikiem, said the responsibility of securing elections could not be left to INEC alone, insisting that the success of the electoral process depended on the collective commitment of all relevant institutions. He emphasised that effective election security required every participating institution to understand and discharge its responsibilities, warning against a fragmented approach to protecting the electoral process. Sinikiem stated, “INEC cannot shoulder the responsibility of conducting elections alone. Election security is a collective responsibility that requires the active participation and commitment of all relevant institutions.” The REC urged members of the committee to strengthen existing partnerships and ensure that potential threats were identified and addressed before they could undermine electoral activities. On his part, the Rivers State Commissioner of Police, Olugbenga Adepoju, assured INEC and other stakeholders of the Nigeria Police Force’s readiness to provide adequate security for electoral activities across the state. Adepoju stressed the importance of strategic deployment of personnel, protection of electoral officials and materials, and sustained security coverage to prevent attacks, intimidation and other forms of electoral interference. He also underscored the need to address security concerns at the grassroots while ensuring adequate protection for INEC offices, facilities and personnel throughout the electoral process. The police chief’s assurance came amid concerns over security challenges that could threaten the conduct of peaceful elections, particularly at the polling unit and ward levels. The Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security is a platform established to facilitate consultation, information sharing and coordinated security responses among INEC, security organisations and relevant government institutions.
